item.title: South Africa rugby names women’s squad for historic Fiji tour
item.description: South Africa has named a 26-player Springbok Women squad for its historic tour of Fiji, where it will face the Rooster Chicken Fijiana XV in two Test matches next month. The Springbok Women will take on Fijiana in Suva on 8 August before the second Test in Lautoka on 15 August, marking the first time the South African women’s team has toured Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
South Africa has named a 26-player Springbok Women squad for its historic tour of Fiji, where it will face the Rooster Chicken Fijiana XV in two Test matches next month.

The Springbok Women will take on Fijiana in Suva on 8 August before the second Test in Lautoka on 15 August, marking the first time the South African women’s team has toured Fiji.

The squad includes the return of experienced No. 8 Aseza Hele, who has been cleared to play after missing recent international fixtures while recovering from hand surgery.

Veteran hooker Lindelwa Gwala also returns after overcoming a calf injury, while Patience Mokone and Zintle Mpupha have been recalled following appearances in the national sevens programme.

Head coach Swys de Bruin has also included two uncapped players, Shiniqwa Lamprecht and Maria Tshiremba, who have transitioned from the Springbok Women’s Sevens programme.

Describing the tour as an important part of South Africa’s preparations, De Bruin said the long journey would provide valuable experience ahead of future international campaigns.

“This will be a challenging trip, but for us in 2026, it is all about pushing beyond comfort zones and, in this case, time zones,” he said.

“It is a long way to travel, but in the wider plan, that is what we will have to do when the next World Cup is played in Australia too.”

De Bruin said he was pleased to welcome experienced players back into the squad while also giving opportunities to emerging talent.

“Both played well on the sevens circuit this year, so I am excited to see their skill set enhancing our style of play,” he said of Lamprecht and Tshiremba.

“Also, Aseza and Lindelwa bring so much experience, which will be needed as we are without some experienced players currently in the rehab programme.”

The Springbok Women will depart for Fiji on Wednesday, with assistant coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September leading the touring squad, while De Bruin remains in Stellenbosch to oversee South Africa’s wider training group.

The two-Test series is expected to provide strong competition for both teams as they continue preparations for future international campaigns.

item.title: Ra beats the odds
item.description: RA head coach Sireli Bobo praised his players for their commitment despite the challenges of assembling the squad after their victory yesterday. Ra and Northland will contest the Vodafone Vanua Cup final after recording impressive victories in their respective semi-finals, with both sides also securing automatic promotion to the 2027 Skipper Cup.
item.content:encoded:
RA head coach Sireli Bobo praised his players for their commitment despite the challenges of assembling the squad after their victory yesterday.

Ra and Northland will contest the Vodafone Vanua Cup final after recording impressive victories in their respective semi-finals, with both sides also securing automatic promotion to the 2027 Skipper Cup.

Ra overturned a halftime deficit to defeat Vatukoula 35-24 in an entertaining contest.

Vatukoula led 14-10 at the break, but Ra came out firing in the second half. A penalty followed by a converted try handed Ra the lead before the side capitalised on its momentum to take control of the match.

A well-executed cross-kick in the closing stages resulted in Ra’s final try, sealing the victory and confirming its place in the championship decider.

“We’ve had our challenges in assembling this team, but the boys have continued to put in the work,” Bobo said.

He said the 30-member squad remained focused throughout the campaign and deserved credit for reaching the final.

Northland, meanwhile, produced a composed second-half performance to defeat Cakaudrove 23-5 after taking a narrow 3-0 lead into halftime.

After a cagey opening spell, Northland raised its intensity after the break, scoring crucial tries while maintaining a solid defensive effort to keep Cakaudrove to just five points.

Captain Osea Turagarua said the team expected a tough contest and prepared accordingly.

“We expected a good fight from Cakaudrove. They are a good team and we also tried to prepare ourselves for that,” Turagarua said.

The victory capped another disciplined performance from Northland, which now shifts its attention to the final against Ra.

With promotion to the Skipper Cup already secured, both teams will now battle for Vanua Cup honours in what promises to be an exciting championship decider.

item.title: Nadi FC eyes IDC qualification
item.description: THE Tagimoucia Nadi FC president Mohammed Rafiq has praised his young side for their determination after producing a spirited performance against the Stratum Construction Rewa FC 1-1 at Prince Charles Park in Nadi on Sunday. Rafiq said the players gave everything on the field and deserved recognition for their commitment.
item.content:encoded:
THE Tagimoucia Nadi FC president Mohammed Rafiq has praised his young side for their determination after producing a spirited performance against the Stratum Construction Rewa FC 1-1 at Prince Charles Park in Nadi on Sunday.

Rafiq said the players gave everything on the field and deserved recognition for their commitment.

“Our players played their hearts out. I must thank my new management and my players for giving their efforts towards a very senior team in Fiji. I must thank them for their brilliant performance,” he said.

Despite the result, Rafiq believes the team remains on track to achieve its main objective of qualifying for the Inter District Championship (IDC).

He said the immediate focus was on the Battle of the Giants (BOG), where the side hoped to build momentum with positive results in the coming weeks.

“We are preparing for BOG first and we aim to win a few more games in the coming weeks to qualify for IDC,” he said.

The club is also set for a major change with experienced football administrator and coach Babs Khan expected to take charge this week after serving as team director for Tailevu Naitasiri.

Rafiq said Khan’s appointment would provide the leadership needed to lift the Green Machine.

“Babs Khan is a Nadi man. He is a strong man who can lead, who can guide and take us forward, which we are looking forward to.”

While acknowledging there are areas that require improvement, Rafiq is confident the coaching staff and senior players will address the team’s shortcomings.

“We are quite adamant on working on our weaknesses. I am sure my team management with the senior players will work on it and try and improve on the weaknesses.”

Rafiq reserved special praise for the club’s sponsors, saying their financial backing has been instrumental in keeping the young side competitive this season.

“A special thanks to our main sponsor, Tagimoucia Grog and Minimart, and co-sponsors Bula Rental and Tours, AAAK Group, Australian Pacific Management Training, Vinay Vikash Hire Truck Services and Signz Creation and Supplies for their continued commitment to the team.”

item.title: Deans heads north
item.description: FOR the first time in the history of the Vodafone Deans competition, Vanua Levu will become the centre of Fiji secondary schools rugby this Saturday, hosting six crucial qualifying matches as the Fiji Rugby Union (FRU) steps up efforts to grow the game beyond its traditional strongholds. All six matches will be hosted at the Ganilau Park in Savusavu.
item.content:encoded:
FOR the first time in the history of the Vodafone Deans competition, Vanua Levu will become the centre of Fiji secondary schools rugby this Saturday, hosting six crucial qualifying matches as the Fiji Rugby Union (FRU) steps up efforts to grow the game beyond its traditional strongholds.

All six matches will be hosted at the Ganilau Park in Savusavu.

FRU acting chief operations officer Talemo Waqa said the move was aimed at ensuring every region shared in the excitement of the country’s premier secondary schools rugby competition.

“We want to encourage movement for development purposes and share the game with all the zones,” Waqa said.

“Sometimes when we overdo it in one area, whether it’s Lautoka or Suva, only the spectators and stakeholders in those areas get to watch the games.”

He said taking the competition to Vanua Levu would allow the communities to experience high-quality schools rugby on their doorstep.

“Now Vanua Levu is bracing itself. They’re getting excited for this week’s games,” he said.

The FRU has also appointed some of Fiji’s most experienced match officials to oversee the fixtures.

Local referee David Vosalevu, who recently returned from officiating at the World Rugby Under-20 Championship, will referee one of the first under-18 playoff game, while fellow senior referee Rasta Rasivhenge will control the second U18 playoff match.

They will be assisted by referee manager James Bolabiu.

Waqa said sending the country’s leading referees to Vanua Levu was another step towards raising the standard and profile of the competition in the North.

“We have confirmed that the top referees will be there,” he said.

“We want to compile that and profile it so you’ll be building the profile of the competition in the North.”

The six matches will mark another milestone in the FRU’s effort to spread the Deans competition beyond its traditional centres, giving Northern schools and supporters the opportunity to host and witness some of the country’s best young rugby talent.

Fixtures at Ganilau Park this Saturday August 01, 2026.

Game 1. 8.30 am – 9.40 am (U15 Third place playoffs) Holy Cross College (N1) v Nasinu Secondary School (S3) – Referee: Seru Tadulala

Game 2. 9.45 am – 11.45 am (U16 Third place playoffs) Saint Bedes College (N1) v Lelean Memorial School (E3) – Referee: Joji C

Game 3. 11.10 am – 12.30 pm (U17 Third place playoff) Batinikama College (N1) v Marist Brothers High School (S3)

Game 4. 12.35 pm – 1.55 pm (U19 Third place playoffs) Navatu Secondary School (N1) v Queen Victoria School (E3)

Game 5. 2 pm – 3.20 pm (U18 Eliminations) Shiri Guru Nanak Khalsa College (N2) v Ratu Navula College (W3)

Game 6. 3:25 pm – 4.45 pm (U18 Eliminations) Navatu Secondary School (N1) v Ra High School (W4)

4. Primary School Students and kids – $3

item.title: Navosa edge Cakaudrove to reach Ranadi Cup final
item.description: NAVOSA has booked its place in the final of the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup after holding off a powerful Cakaudrove side for a thrilling 33-31 victory in their Ranadi semi-final clash at the HFC Bank Stadium. Cakaudrove took control early, racing to a 19-7 halftime lead through disciplined defence and a well-executed attack.
item.content:encoded:
NAVOSA has booked its place in the final of the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup after holding off a powerful Cakaudrove side for a thrilling 33-31 victory in their Ranadi semi-final clash at the HFC Bank Stadium.

Cakaudrove took control early, racing to a 19-7 halftime lead through disciplined defence and a well-executed attack.

While the side carried the momentum into the second spell, Navosa began perfectly with a converted try narrowing the points gap giving the side a significant boost.

Cakaudrove, however, refused to go away. It mounted a spirited comeback, going neck to neck against Navosa to close gap and set up tense finish.

Despite the late challenge from Cakaudrove, Navosa stayed calm in the final minutes to hold off the late comeback, winning 33-31 to reach the final.

Captain of the Navosa side, Maria Nauvasi credits her team for the hard work they put in allowing them to secure a spot in the final.

Nauvasi also shared despite the challenges the team faced, they delivered a spectacular performance.

“I thank the girls for the hard work they have put in,” Nauvasi said.

“At times we faced challenges at camp, but I thank God for giving us the victory.”

The captain also expressed gratitude to the supporters for coming out in numbers and showing their support to the team.

“Thank you to our supporters for coming out in numbers and cheering us out.”

Meanwhile in the other Ranadi semi-finals Yasawa thrashed Northern Bulls 90-17 booking their finals berth with a statement of intent.

The two team’s will meet in the finals next week and will also progress to next year’s top tier competition the Marama Cup.

In the Vanua Cup U20 semi-finals Cakaudrove edged Northland 23-16, while Macuata overcame a spirited Coastland side 39-32.

This sets the stage for a northern finals showdown in next week between Macuata and Cakaudrove.

item.title: Top Drua Women honours tonight
item.description: The McDonald’s Fiji Fijian Drua Women will celebrate another memorable Super Rugby Women’s campaign when the club hosts its annual awards ceremony at the Sofitel Fiji Resort and Spa tonight. Six major awards will be presented during the evening, honouring excellence both on and off the field.
item.content:encoded:
The McDonald’s Fiji Fijian Drua Women will celebrate another memorable Super Rugby Women’s campaign when the club hosts its annual awards ceremony at the Sofitel Fiji Resort and Spa tonight.

Six major awards will be presented during the evening, honouring excellence both on and off the field.

The awards include Rookie of the Year, Community Champion, Players’ Player of the Year, Fan Player of the Year, Try of the Year, and the prestigious Player of the Year award.

The Rookie of the Year accolade will recognise the season’s most impressive newcomer.

The Community Champion award will honour the player who has made the greatest impact through community engagement and inspiring the next generation of rugby players.

The Players’ Player of the Year, voted by teammates, is expected to be one of the night’s most coveted honours, reflecting the respect earned within the squad. Fans will also have their say through the Fan Player of the Year award, celebrating the player who captured the hearts of Drua supporters throughout the season.

The spectacular Try of the Year award will recognise the team’s best five-pointer of the campaign, while the evening will conclude with the announcement of the McDonald’s Fiji Fijian Drua Women’s Player of the Year, recognising the standout performer across the entire season.

The awards night recognises the outstanding performances and contributions that shaped the Drua Women’s impressive 2026 season, which culminated in a second consecutive appearance in the Super Rugby Women’s grand final.

item.title: Brad Mooar appointed new Fijian Drua head coach
item.description: The Fijian Drua have appointed highly regarded New Zealand coach Brad Mooar as Head Coach of the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua Men ahead of the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season. Mooar, who has signed a two-year contract, will officially join the club in September 2026 to oversee preparations for the new campaign.
item.content:encoded:
The Fijian Drua have appointed highly regarded New Zealand coach Brad Mooar as Head Coach of the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua Men ahead of the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season.

Mooar, who has signed a two-year contract, will officially join the club in September 2026 to oversee preparations for the new campaign.

He arrives with an impressive coaching résumé, having helped guide the Crusaders to three consecutive Super Rugby titles, served as an assistant coach with the All Blacks and Scotland, and previously led Welsh club Scarlets.

His appointment follows what the Drua described as an extensive international recruitment process involving Fijian Drua and Fiji Rugby leadership, along with an independent expert.

Fijian Drua Chief Executive Officer Jeff Miller said Mooar emerged as the standout candidate from a highly competitive field.

“This is one of the most important appointments in the short history of the Fijian Drua and we were determined to conduct a genuinely exhaustive process.”

Miller said the club received applications from an outstanding group of coaches but Mooar distinguished himself through his technical expertise, player development credentials and leadership qualities.

“Brad stood out through his technical and tactical knowledge, his experience in championship-winning environments, his understanding of player development and, importantly, his ability to build strong relationships.”

He added that Mooar understands the responsibility that comes with coaching Fiji’s Super Rugby franchise.

“Our purpose is to win Super Rugby Pacific, inspire a nation and change lives for the better. He has embraced that responsibility and we firmly believe Brad is the right person to lead the next phase of our journey.”

Mooar said he was honoured to take on one of the Southern Hemisphere’s most unique coaching roles.

“It’s a tremendous honour to be given the opportunity to lead the Drua and coach Fiji’s team in Super Rugby Pacific.”

He said the opportunity to work with Fijian players and culture was a major attraction.

“What drew me to this role is the chance to work with such wonderful athletes, to be part of a culture and a people I deeply admire, and to help build something meaningful for the nation.”

Mooar said his goal is to build a team capable of playing an exciting brand of rugby while competing for championships.

“We want to inspire the country, win championships and continue to grow our people and the game in Fiji by creating something the country can be truly proud of.”

He also congratulated the McDonald’s Fiji Drua Women, who recently secured the 2026 Super Rugby Women’s minor premiership and earned the right to host the Grand Final.

Mooar is currently an assistant coach with the Crusaders, having returned to the franchise in 2025 after previously helping the club win Super Rugby titles in 2017, 2018 and 2019.

His coaching career has also included roles with the Scarlets, the All Blacks, Scotland, the Southern Kings, Eastern Province Kings, and Southland. A former Mid Canterbury first five-eighth, Mooar is also a qualified lawyer.

The Drua said further announcements regarding the men’s coaching staff will be made in due course.

item.title: Star emerges
item.description: LELEAN Memorial School fullback Ratu Apenisa Nayalatabua Navikutu is open to considering an overseas rugby contract if the opportunity arises after his outstanding performance in the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Under-18 Dean’s final. Navikutu made the comments after being asked whether he would consider moving overseas if the Fijian Drua did not offer him a contract.
item.content:encoded:
LELEAN Memorial School fullback Ratu Apenisa Nayalatabua Navikutu is open to considering an overseas rugby contract if the opportunity arises after his outstanding performance in the Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Under-18 Dean’s final.

Navikutu made the comments after being asked whether he would consider moving overseas if the Fijian Drua did not offer him a contract.

The man-of-the-match was instrumental in LMS’s 29-17 victory over Ratu Kadavulevu School on Saturday, producing a near-perfect performance with the boot – converting eight penalties – while directing play from the back.

“If an opportunity comes, whether it’s in Fiji or overseas, I’ll sit down with my family and carefully consider all the options before making a decision on what’s best for my future,” he said.

Navikutu admitted he did not expect to finish the final with eight successful penalty goals.

“I honestly didn’t expect to kick that many penalties. During the game I just shut out all the noise, focused on each kick and made sure I got the ball over,” he said.

His accurate kicking proved decisive, stretching LMS’s lead to 18-5 at halftime with another penalty on the stroke of the break.

However, the talented fullback’s influence extended beyond his goal-kicking.

He orchestrated LMS’s attacking structure, organised the defensive line and produced three try-saving tackles to deny RKS during its second-half fightback.

His all-round display has prompted calls from rugby followers for the Fijian Drua to monitor the emerging playmaker closely before overseas clubs secure his services.

Navikutu’s rise has been rapid. He joined LMS this year after transferring from Nakasi High School.

Before arriving at LMS, he played senior division club rugby for Lokia village in Rewa, an experience he credited with preparing him for this year’s schools campaign.

“I’m grateful to Lelean Memorial School for believing in me and giving me the opportunity to showcase my rugby,” he said.

Originally from Navolau, Rakiraki, Ra, with maternal links to Lokia in Rewa, Navikutu has emerged as one of the standout performers of this year’s Eastern Zone competition.

Following his man-of-the-match display, his rugby future appears brighter than ever.
